content:
Hi, I am new to Lean and I am using it, as recommended on the website, with the VS Code extension. I would like to know whether there is any way to make the editor automatically scaffold the subgoal structure in cases where a tactic results in several subgoals.

For example, whenever I use the apply tactic, say, on a function f : a -> b -> c, I tend to automatically write the following code (pardon the lack of proper unicode syntax):

apply f
. show a
  sorry
. show b
  sorry

I then focus on the first sorry and start filling the proof from there. Doing this manually is, however, tedious. Is there anything I can do to automate it? I looked at the configuration options of the Lean 4 VS Code extension and I didn't really see anything relevant there.

e.g.

example : 1 = 1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  -- place the cursor anywhere on this line and press `Ctrl+.` / `Cmd+.`
Huh, it works, thanks! It would be great if it put the shows there as well, but this is better than nothing for sure
It is redundant for writing the proof, yes, but I like it there just for the readability I would say...

Umm I'm sure it can be added, but you'd have to keep the code-action in your own repo
Also I'd bet it will fail 90% of the time for the same reasons that extract_goal fails; the pretty-printer doesn't produce valid code

Oh, I see... I will learn to live without shows then I guess. It's just that I am going through Mathematics in Lean, saw the show there, and thought it was neat (I have some previous experience with Coq code from Software Foundations and the proof scripts always seemed unreadable to me there).
